RFC2545-3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c19 judge). (a) forbidden: a Next Hop field whose first address is not the global next hop, a link-local second address placed first, a non-link-local second address, a second address appended unconditionally, or a second address that is not the next hop's own (the speaker's Link-Local after another router's global). (b) conf-llnh-update.ci and adj-rib-in-replay-rfc2545-next-hop.ci pin global-then-link-local by exact wire hex (offset order); TestSendAnnounceRefusesUnusableIPv6NextHop requires ErrNextHopUnencodable and empty wire for an IPv4 or unset address in the global slot; TestSessionSendAnnounceRefusesNonLinkLocalSecondAddress requires the same for a global second address; new-v6.ci pins the one-address form when no link-local exists. NEW negative TestOwnLinkLocalNotPairedWithAnotherRoutersGlobalOnTheSharedLink (sendStaticRoutes, one-hop internal peer, explicit next hop 2001:db8:1::99 on the shared link) asserts Contains the 16-octet ::99 attribute AND NotContains [::99, fe80::1]; it was observed red as the c18 probe before the R55 fix and carries a record on classify. Fixture positives (conf-llnh-update.conf local-address fd00::2 = next hop; interop fd00:1e:0::2 held on the lab interface) keep a speaker-own global, so the fix leaves them valid by reading; their re-run is owed to the functional/interop gates.

RFC2545-3-2.note: (a) forbidden: a length octet other than 16 with only a global address, or other than 32 with a link-local also included. (b) new-v6.ci asserts 800E26 0002 01 10 with one 16-octet address; conf-llnh-update.ci and adj-rib-in-replay-rfc2545-next-hop.ci assert the 0x20 octet with both addresses by exact hex; TestSessionSendAnnounceRefusesNonLinkLocalSecondAddress asserts no 32-octet field is written for a non-link-local second address.

RFC2545-3-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c19 judge) after the RFC2545-3-6 split: this row now carries the include half for a global that is the speaker's own address and the exclude half. (a) forbidden: including the link-local address when either half of the condition fails, or omitting it when both hold for the speaker's own global. (b) conf-llnh-update.ci (local-address fd00::2 = next hop) and TestSendAnnounceAppendsLinkLocalWhenSection3Holds / TestDefaultOriginateAppendsLinkLocalWhenSection3Holds assert the 32-octet form when both halves hold; conf-llnh-lla-only.ci asserts the 16-octet form when the global next hop is on no connected subnet; TestSendAnnounceOmitsLinkLocalWhenPeerOffLink / TestDefaultOriginateOmitsLinkLocalWhenPeerOffLink assert the 16-octet form and NotContains the 32-octet one when the peer half fails; checkRFC2545NextHops proves both against FRR. Both halves are broken separately. Note: the speaker's own Link-Local is supplied by the session > link-local leaf (YANG says set it on a shared-link session); with no leaf Ze includes none.

RFC2545-3-4.note: (a) forbidden: a second address or a length other than 16 when the inclusion condition does not hold. (b) TestSendAnnounceOmitsLinkLocalWhenPeerOffLink asserts the global-only form with length 0x10 and NotContains the 32-octet form; new-v6.ci pins 01 10 plus one address byte for byte; conf-llnh-update.ci is the negative, asserting the field is not reduced to 16 while the condition holds.

RFC2545-3-6.note: Judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c19 judge). Split from RFC2545-3-3 under R3/R55(a); the quote is the whole Section 3 iff sentence, which coincides with the clause. Gap confirmed at the producer: linkScope.linkLocalNextHop appends the configured Link-Local only for nextHopRouterSpeaker (nextHopOwners.classify: session endpoint, configured local address, held interface address), so a next hop Ze WRITES that names another router on a subnet shared with the speaker and the peer (explicit next hop, static or API route) goes as the 16-octet global alone, where Section 3 asks for 'the link-local IPv6 address of the next hop'. Ze has no source for that router's Link-Local on these rails. Annotation imprecision (reported to main thread, not fixed by the judge): on the relay rail with next hop unchanged/auto (precomputeNextHop nhModeNone) the received field passes verbatim, so a 32-octet field the source sent does carry the third party's own Link-Local; the gap is the rails where Ze writes the next hop, not 'Ze learns no other router's Link-Local'.
